question: You are working with a dataset containing two numerical variables. The data includes noise and some extreme values. You want to examine whether these two variables are related, even if the relationship might be non-linear. Which type of visualization would be the most appropriate?
options: Histogram
Boxplot
Scatter plot
Bar chart
correct: Scatter plot

question: What is polynomial feature expansion?
options: Creating new features by combining existing features
Transforming categorical variables into numeric representations
Generating higher-degree terms for numeric features
Providing degree terms for numeric features
correct: Generating higher-degree terms for numeric features

question: What is log transformation commonly used for?
options: Handling missing values in numeric features
Reducing the impact of outliers in skewed distributions
Converting categorical features into numeric features
Converting numerical features into categorical features
correct: Reducing the impact of outliers in skewed distributions

question: What is the major purpose of distance metrics in clustering?
options: To measure the physical distance between data points
To quantify the similarity or dissimilarity between data points
To determine the direction of data points
To classify data points into predefined clusters
correct: To quantify the similarity or dissimilarity between data points

question: What is the main condition to use stacking as ensemble method?
options: Models need to be parametric
Models need to be nonparametric
Models need to output residual values for each class
Models need to output predicted probabilities
correct: Models need to output predicted probabilities

question: What is a hyperplane in the context of SVM?
options: A plane that separates the data into two classes
A line that connects support vectors
A subspace of lower dimensionality
The axis of the highest variance in the data
correct: A plane that separates the data into two classes

question: What is the role of the regularization parameter in the regularization process?
options: It controls the overall strength of regularization
It sets the learning rate for the optimization algorithm
It defines the number of iterations in model training
It has no impact on regularization
correct: It controls the overall strength of regularization

question: What is the purpose of point estimation in statistics?
options: To estimate a range of values for a parameter
To summarize the central tendency of a dataset
To provide a single value as the best guess for a parameter
To assess the variability of a dataset
correct: To provide a single value as the best guess for a parameter

question: What is the main objective of using ensemble methods such as bagging and boosting, in the case of imbalanced classes?
options: To decrease the model's accuracy
To increase the model's complexity
To improve the model's generalization and handling of imbalanced data
To reduce the impact of the majority class
correct: To improve the model's generalization and handling of imbalanced data

question: What is one of the real-world solutions to fix the problems of the curse dimensionality?
options: Increase the size of the data set
Use more computational power
Reduce the dimension of the data set.
Balance the classes of a data set
correct: Reduce the dimension of the data set.

question: What is artificial intelligence?
options: A subset of deep learning.
Any program that can sense, reason, act, and adapt.
A subset of machine learning
None of the others
correct: Any program that can sense, reason, act, and adapt.

question: What is the main goal of unsupervised learning?
options: Predicting a target variable
Classifying data into predefined categories
Discovering patterns and structures in data
Evaluating model accuracy
correct: Discovering patterns and structures in data

question: What is the purpose of using bootstrapping in the Bagging algorithm?
options: To reduce overfitting
To create diverse subsets of the dataset
To increase the number of features
To speed up the training process
correct: To create diverse subsets of the dataset

question: What are the Weaknesses of the Mean shift method?
options: Result depends on window size (bandwidth)
Selection of window size is not easy
Does not assume number or shape of clusters
Robust to outliers
correct: Result depends on window size (bandwidth)
Selection of window size is not easy

question: What does the test set represent in machine learning?
options: The part of the data used for model training
A set of examples the model has already seen during training
New, unseen data the model has not encountered during training
A set of data reserved for validation purposes
correct: New, unseen data the model has not encountered during training

question: What are the strengths of the Mean shift algorithm?
options: Model-free: does not assume number or shape of clusters
Can use just one parameter: window size (bandwidth)
Robust to outliers
All of these
correct: All of these

question: What are "core points" in the DBSCAN algorithm?
options: Core points are outliers that do not belong to any cluster
Core points are data points that has at least a minimum number of other points (minPts) within a specified distance (epsilon) from it
Core points are data points that are isolated from the rest of the dataset
Core points are centroids of the clusters identified by DBSCAN
correct: Core points are data points that has at least a minimum number of other points (minPts) within a specified distance (epsilon) from it

question: What are polynomial features?
options: They are higher order relationships in the data.
They are logistic regression coefficients.
They are lower order relationships in the data.
They are represented by linear relationships in the data.
correct: They are higher order relationships in the data.

question: What are the two main data problems companies face when getting started with artificial intelligence/machine learning?
options: Data sampling and categorization
Outliers and duplicated data
Lack of relevant data and bad data
Lack of training and expertise
correct: Lack of relevant data and bad data

question: What does the hyperparameter "alpha" control in Elastic Net regularization?
options: Overall strength of regularization
Balance between L1 and L2 penalties
Learning rate of the optimization algorithm
Number of iterations in model training
correct: Overall strength of regularization

question: What does the term "precision" measure in the context of classification metrics?
options: The ability to correctly identify positive instances
The ability to correctly identify negative instances
The proportion of actual positive instances correctly identified
The trade-off between precision and recall
correct: The ability to correctly identify positive instances

question: Which of the following is an example of feature engineering?
options: Importing libraries in Python
Standardizing numeric features
Creating a new feature based on existing ones
All of these
correct: Creating a new feature based on existing ones

question: Which of the following statements is a characteristic of the DBSCAN algorithm?
options: Can handle tons of data and weird shapes.
Finds uneven cluster sizes (one is big, some are tiny).
It will do a great performance finding many clusters.
It will do a great performance finding few clusters.
correct: Can handle tons of data and weird shapes.

question: When is it most likely that an observation contains an outlier for one of its features?
options: One feature has an internally studentized residual value above 3.
One feature has a deleted residual value above 3.
The observation consists of the maximum target value.
The observation is missing values for several of the features.
correct: One feature has an internally studentized residual value above 3.

question: When using DBSCAN, how does the algorithm determine that a cluster is complete and is time to move to a different point of the data set and potentially start a new cluster?
options: When the algorithm requires you to change the input.
When the algorithm forms a new cluster using the outliers.
When no point is left unvisited by the chain reaction.
When the solution converges to a single cluster.
correct: When no point is left unvisited by the chain reaction.
